title: Crest Passed at 23.5 ft: Now Plan the Return

fields.headline: River crests at 23.5 ft, now falling
fields.narration:
It is now 15:00 CDT, Saturday 24 April 2027. The Cedar River crested at Cedar Ford overnight and is now falling slowly. At 15:00, CFDI4 on the Route 38 bridge piers reads 23.1 ft. The levee held. The ringed boil at Station 18+50 is still under 24-hour watch, and Pump Stations 1 and 2 are still running. Cedar Hollow is still under water, every closed road is still closed, and the crews are on their fourth day. At 12:20 the EOC received this product:

TEST...FLOOD WARNING...TEST
NATIONAL WEATHER SERVICE QUAD CITIES IA/IL
1200 PM CDT SAT APR 24 2027
...THIS IS AN EXERCISE MESSAGE...
THE FLOOD WARNING CONTINUES FOR THE CEDAR RIVER AT CEDAR FORD (CFDI4).
* WHAT CHANGED...THE RIVER CRESTED AT 23.5 FEET AT 5:45 AM SATURDAY, NEAR THE FORECAST OF 23.4 FEET, AND IS NOW FALLING.
* AT 11:00 AM SATURDAY THE STAGE WAS 23.2 FEET.
* MAJOR FLOODING IS OCCURRING.
* FORECAST...THE RIVER WILL FALL BELOW 23.0 FEET THIS EVENING, BELOW 19.0 FEET LATE MONDAY, AND BELOW FLOOD STAGE WEDNESDAY.
...TEST...$$

Since then, four more messages have reached the EOC.
keyFacts: USACE Rock Island District geotechnical engineer, email to the Levee District Superintendent, cc TCEMA, 13:05: "The ringed boil at 18+50 is running clear at reduced flow. Keep the ring and 24-hour patrol until the stage is below 19.0 ft. We recommend a post-flood inspection of the Hollow Creek reach."
Phone call, 13:40, Hollow Court Care Center Administrator Rosa Delgado: "Meadowview wants my 36 back Monday. When can I go home?"
Iowa HSEMD regional duty officer, WebEOC message, 14:10: "Please submit initial damage assessment numbers for Cedar Hollow and the levee by 18:00 for the declaration package."
Post, @HollowCtMom, Cedar Ford Neighbors Facebook group, 14:32: "River's going down, why can't we go home TODAY?? #CedarFordFlood" (85 shares, 210 comments)
fields.expectedAction: EM starts damage assessment in Cedar Hollow and on the levee, sends HSEMD the initial numbers by 18:00, and plans a phased return tied to the stage. Residents go back first, after the water drops and homes are inspected. Hollow Court goes back last, after the utility and road checks. PW keeps every road closed until it has been inspected (SFMECS 4). LEV keeps the ring and the 24-hour patrol in place. WWTP reports the plant status and any bypass to Iowa DNR through the EOC. PIO announces the 23.5 ft crest at 05:45, gives the falling forecast and its 12:00 Saturday issuance, and says no one goes back before the inspections.
fields.facilitatorNote: This is the final row before ENDEX. Do not announce the hot wash yet. The plan's reentry rule (SFMECS 3, step 6) is below 17.0 ft and falling, plus the Fire Chief's utility check and the Building Official's inspection. If players promise a return 'once it's under 19 ft' or give a date, ask which forecast issuance and which stage they are using. A Monday return for Hollow Court conflicts with the forecast, which has the river still above 19.0 ft until late Monday.
fields.scenarioTitle: Eighteen Hours — Rising Crest, Evacuation Clock & Levee Fight

instructorNote: This inject moves the exercise from response to recovery. Watch whether the Coordinator ties every return decision to a stage and the inspections from the plan, rather than to a date or public pressure, and whether the PIO's message names the crest and the issuance. Also check that the HSEMD numbers go out before the 18:00 deadline.
